body: Supercell’s long-in-gestation action RPG spin-off of Clash of Clans seems to be edging closer to launch: the Finnish firm is opening a beta test for Project Rise beginning August 19, which runs until September 2.
The project was first revealed as Clash Heroes way back in 2021, but it was rebooted and renamed in 2024 as Project Rise. There’s been very little news on the title since.
Snapshot Games’ mobile port of Purple Lamp’s 3D platformer remake launches on iOS and Android on September 16, priced at $15.99. It’s now open for pre-orders.
Mintrocket’s hit RPG-management sim launches on iOS and Android on September 17, complete with the Dredge and In the Jungle DLC packs included at launch.

articles.title: Supercell says Mo.co unlikely to be cancelled despite major changes ahead
articles.summary: Supercell has revealed that cancelling Mo.co remains unlikely despite the game underperforming against expectations as the developer prepares further major changes to its gameplay.
body: Three months after the game's relaunch, Supercell said the latest data shows its gameplay loop “quickly gets stale” for most players, causing them to drop off.
However, players who remain are spending unusually long periods in the game, the studio claims, suggesting Mo.co currently works well for a niche audience but is not ready to scale.

“Now, this won’t be fixed with small changes," said Supercell in a post. “We’re already prototyping and testing big and exciting stuff. With that being said, all the effort being relocated into developing and iterating those new features will come at an unfortunate yet unavoidable cost.
“Team members who usually dedicate their time to building all-new seasonal events, monsters, and weapons will now focus on developing those much-needed changes."

articles.title: Mo Co is underperforming and will be rebooted (again) – but Supercell says killing it is “unlikely”
articles.summary: Supercell has floated the possibility of killing its monster hunting game Mo Co after a recent reboot underperformed – but closing the game entirely “remains an unlikely scenario,” says the Finnish firm.
body: Three months after the monster hunting game was effectively relaunched, the development team has updated players on how it’s going: “mo.co is not performing as well as we hoped,” the blog reads.

“While some aspects, such as the new weapons and gameplay changes are promising, the gameplay loop quickly gets stale for most of our players, leading them to drop off. On the other hand, the average gameplay time for those who are staying is unusually high. This shows that mo.co is working quite well for a niche, but it’s not yet ready to scale up.”
There will now be further changes to the game which will disrupt the next season, and likely the one after that.

The blog continues: “You may be wondering about the future of the game. Could it be killed? That still remains an unlikely scenario. We have lots of ideas we’re excited about, and we fully believe in mo.co’s potential. However, we need to be open and transparent about the possibility.”
